Multi-layered inspection

The 3-Layer Hybrid Threat Detection Architecture

Layer 1 (Signatures): Ultra-fast deterministic rule check mapping ports heuristics and Zeek/Suricata alerts.
Layer 2 (Ensemble ML Stacking): Advanced stacking model (XGBoost + Random Forest) providing 98.8% classification precision.
Layer 3 (GenAI Analyst): Local pipeline triggering Qwen 2.5 / Llama 3.3 analyst logs, MITRE mappings, and auto-generated rules.
Core Presentation Takeaway

Combining signature speed, statistical machine learning weights, and linguistic LLM reasoning achieves defense-in-depth.

Layer 2 Performance metrics

Stacking Classifier Validation: XGBoost Confusion Matrix

Evaluates the mathematical precision of our Layer 2 XGBoost stacking baseline across 102,398 network flow samples.
Identifies 16,910 true positive attacks and classifies 84,294 normal benign network operations flawlessly.
Limits system false positives to a minimal 289 instances, ensuring high trust and preventing accidental server lockdown.
Core Presentation Takeaway

The stacking classifier achieves a high 98.8% recall. Out of thousands of active attacks, the failure leak rate is confined to ~0.5%.

Model Confusion Matrix (real_source: confusion_matrix.png)
Telemetry Feature Importance

Diagnostic Feature Importances & Scapy Interfaces

Ranks flow characteristics by their influence weights: destination port (dst_port) leads with a high 33% importance score.
Size metrics, including packet-to-byte-ratio (31%) and bytes-per-packet (8%), populate the high-influence boundaries.
Integrates with workspace compiler hooks (ids_check.py) confirming Python Scapy, Numpy, XGBoost, and Joblib are fully bound.
Core Presentation Takeaway

Connection metadata dictates over 60% of classifier decisions. This enables SudoSOC to spot suspicious TLS/SSL reverse shells without payload decryption.

Live real-time monitoring

Live Operations Console: Streamlit Dashboard Live Alerts

Active visual representation of the product UI running on port 8501, aggregating network packets dynamically.
Logs flow records (timestamp, ports, protocol) and flags attack classes (including MAILBOMB, EXPLOIT, and GUESS_PASSWORD).
Live telemetry metrics reveal Recent Alerts (200), Blocked IPs (25), and Critical Alerts (14) at a single glance.
Core Presentation Takeaway

Converts raw JSONL sniffer logs into actionable threat telemetry, demonstrating real-time prevention blocks in under 3 seconds.

Live Operations Alert Feed Console (Streamlit Port 8501)
Adaptive retraining engine

Continuous Online Learning & Concept Drift Monitor

Integrates drift monitoring tools, tracking baseline drift indexes (KL-Divergence) dynamically against 1.15 million trained samples.
Concept drift is validated within thresholds (0.04 drift value vs 0.15 automatic incremental retrain trigger).
Queues pending analyst feedback logs (380 samples) allowing human-in-the-loop tags to adjust stacking models live.
Core Presentation Takeaway

SudoSOC mitigates baseline decay. The continuous online loop guarantees the classifier adapts to changing signature techniques over time.

Online Learning & Concept Drift Telemetry
Analyst-in-the-loop response

Adaptive Response Engine & Human Feedback Console

Automated response actions distributed across ISOLATE (24%), RATE_LIMIT (69%), and AUTO_BLOCK (7%) policies.
Analyst verdict panel allows manual override: False Positive (NORMAL) or True Positive (confirm) with notes.
Manual ISOLATE / RELEASE source IP controls enable direct intervention even when ML confidence is low.
Core Presentation Takeaway

True autonomous defense requires human oversight. SudoSOC's feedback loop refines the model while giving analysts full override authority.

Adaptive Response Distribution & Analyst Override
Production-grade deployment

Real Engine Deployment & Technology Stack

Engine deployed locally via Python runtime with Scapy real-time packet capture on live network interfaces (NPF devices).
Streamlit dashboard serves the operational SOC console on localhost:8501 with live auto-refreshing alert feeds.
GenAI layer connects via HuggingFace Inference API to Qwen 2.5 / Llama 3.3 models for intelligent threat summarization.
Core Presentation Takeaway

SudoSOC runs on commodity hardware with zero cloud dependency. Every component is validated and confirmed operational in the terminal.

Real Engine Startup & Package Verification Terminal
Market positioning

SudoSOC vs. Industry Competitors

Traditional IDS tools (Snort, Suricata) rely exclusively on static signature rules with no machine learning or adaptive capabilities.
Enterprise solutions (Darktrace, CrowdStrike) offer ML detection but lack open-source transparency and local GenAI integration.
SudoSOC uniquely combines all three layers — signatures, ML stacking, and GenAI analysis — in a single open-source package.
Core Presentation Takeaway

No existing tool combines all three detection layers with open-source access, adaptive learning, and GenAI-powered analysis in one engine.
